title: Warm Pillowy Venezuelan Pepper Empanadas
description: A lacto-vegetarian friendly solo dinner dish featuring sweet peppadew peppers and shio-koji cure, these empanadas are fatty and pillowy, perfect for a warm evening meal.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, salt, sugar, and yeast.
Add cold butter to the dry ingredients and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, and shio-koji.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Flatten each ball into a disk shape and place a few slices of peppadew peppers in the center of each disk.
Fold the dough over the peppers to form a half moon shape and press the edges together to seal the empanada.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with olive oil and bake for 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
